title: Transient Burst Exchange & SLA Smoothing — PRD (draft)
content:
Executive summary:

This doc proposes a new Dedicated-capacity feature set: a transient burst exchange and SLA smoothing model that lets committed tenants consume short-term excess capacity while preserving predictable latencies and isolation guarantees for paying customers. The goal is to increase utilization of reserved pools (raise revenue-per-GPU) and reduce customer-visible throttles during short surges, without creating noisy-neighbor risk or exposing owners to hard SLA violations.

Context and motivation:
- Dedicated pools frequently have short-lived slack (minutes-to-hours) caused by natural variability in tenant workloads, rollouts, and maintenance windows.
- Current options are coarse: hard reservation (wastes capacity) or wide burst windows (risk impacting SLAs).
- Customers want predictable percentiles (p50/p95/p99 tail latency) and simple billing, while sales asks for mechanisms to sell excess capacity.

Problem statement:
- How do we let teams safely sell/route transient capacity to secondary consumers without introducing preemptive failures for primary tenants or opaque billing surprises?
- How can infra autoscaling and burst policies be combined so the system gracefully degrades across tenants when capacity is constrained, and recovers quickly?

Goals (primary):
- Allow short-duration burst tenancy for opportunistic users while keeping tail latency degradation for committed tenants bounded (configurable).
- Provide transparent accounting and simple unit economics for burst usage (e.g., minute-level metering).
- Offer operator controls for eviction granularity, preemption windows, and automatic spill policies.
- Maintain observability at token/request and tenant levels for debugging regressions.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the Dedicated reservation model. This is additive: optional add-on for customers who want to monetize spare capacity or accept low-tier burst consumers.
- Solving cross-region capacity routing in this phase. Focus is on single-pool behavior.

Success metrics (SLOs and product KPIs):
- Commitment SLO: committed tenants see <10% relative increase in p95 latency under typical burst loads (configurable).
- Utilization: raise average GPU utilization on targeted pools by +8–15% in Q1 pilot customers.
- Revenue: generate incremental burst revenue equal to >= 3% of Dedicated ARR for pilot pools.
- Operational: fewer than 2 Sev2 incidents attributable to burst logic in first 3 months.

User personas:
- Platform owner (tenant): wants predictable latency and clear controls for eviction/fidelity.
- Burst consumer (secondary): wants low-cost, short-lived capacity for non-critical workloads (batch, background embeddings, non-customer facing jobs).
- Operator/SRE: needs safe defaults and clear runbooks to respond to misbehaving tenants or oversubscription.

Constraints and assumptions:
- Hardware: pools are homogeneous per reservation (same GPU class).
- Billing granularity: minute-level metering for burst usage is acceptable for pilot.
- Compatibility: must interoperate with existing autoscaler and fallback policies (model variants).

Design overview (concepts):
1) Capacity classes
- Guaranteed: the reservation committed to the tenant; strict isolation for baseline requests (critical routes).
- Smoothing buffer: small soft margin above guaranteed capacity used to absorb microbursts without preemption. Config per-tenant as percent of reservation (default 5%).
- Transient/brokered: opportunistic capacity that can be leased for short windows; preemptible within preemption window.

2) Burst brokerage (exchange)
- Tenants can opt their unused capacity into a pool for transient leases (opt-in at pool level).
- Ledger model: each participating tenant publishes an envelope (available units, max preemption frequency, min retained buffer). System aggregates envelopes to form brokered supply.
- Lease semantics: short time-boxed leases (1–30 minutes) with preemption notice (delta ms to seconds) depending on route criticality.
- Pricing: market is fixed-price (pilot) with dynamic multiplier when supply scarcity crosses thresholds. Billing shows minute-resolution usage and tenant attribution.

3) SLA smoothing
- Smoothing window: requests are allowed to burst into the smoothing buffer for short periods; background score-based admission decider favors low-latency tail preservation.
- Adaptive degradation: when contention increases, the system performs graded actions in this order:
  a) throttle new best-effort leases (no new burst starts)
  b) shrink smoothing buffer for all tenants by a configurable percent
  c) preempt transient leases older than threshold
  d) preempt lower-priority committed routes (if tenant opted for managed-fidelity)
- Tail protection: token-level latency tracking triggers emergency rollback to hard isolation if p99 rises past configured bound for > X minutes.

4) Isolation controls and tenant fidelity profiles
- Fidelity levels for committed tenants (customer-facing):
  - High-fidelity: never preempt, minimal smoothing buffer (default for SLA plans).
  - Standard: allow smoothing buffer and controlled preemption of committed low-priority routes (e.g., background embeddings).
  - Open: tenant accepts preemption for specified routes and can receive cost credits.
- Admin APIs expose per-route flags (critical, best-effort, preemptible) to map application traffic to fidelity tiers.

5) Autoscaler interaction
- Autoscaler is made burst-aware: it treats smoothing buffer as non-guaranteed and uses a predictive headroom model to avoid oscillation.
- When sustained load persists above a threshold, system converts brokered transient usage into a scale signal to spin up more Dedicated capacity (if customer has burst-buy options) or to set a preferred fallback.

API and UX (customer-facing):
- Console toggle: "Enable transient leasing" with simple sliders: max percent of pool, max lease duration, preemption notice.
- Route map: UI to classify routes into fidelity bands (drag-and-drop).
- Billing page: minute-by-minute audit for burst consumption with tenant attribution and cost per minute.
- CLI/SDK: lease API (CreateLease, QueryLease, CancelLease), route tagging, and fidelity policy endpoints.

Operator/Runbook features:
- Admin override to instantly drain brokered leases from a pool (force reclaim).
- Read-only dashboards showing ledger supply-demand, eviction rate, and top preempted leases.
- Alerts: sustained p99 degradation, rapid churn of leases, or ledger inconsistency.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit per-tenant metrics: guaranteed_utilization, smoothing_buffer_usage, transient_lease_count, preemptions/sec, lease_latency_impact.
- Traces: attach lease_id to request traces for postmortems.
- Audit logs: who opted-in/opted-out, lease creation/deletion, preemption events.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal): simulate brokerage in staging using shadow mode (no actual preemption).
- Phase 1 (pilot): 2–3 trusted customers opt-in on non-critical pools; monitoring and manual rollback enabled.
- Phase 2 (wider): add console controls and billing integration; open to customers by request.

Risks and mitigations:
- Noisy neighbor risk: mitigate via conservative default smoothing buffers and per-tenant isolation caps.
- Billing disputes: mitigate with per-minute audit logs and clear cost rules in contract.
- Autoscaler oscillation: mitigate by treating smoothing buffer as soft capacity and using predictive headroom.

Open questions for product/eng alignment:
- Pricing model: fixed discount vs dynamic market; what price sensitivity do customers show?
- Preemption notice latency: how much notice do top-tier latency-sensitive apps require? (ms vs seconds)
- Minimum lease unit: 1 minute or 30-second granularity?
- Contract/legal: wording for opt-in and liability for preemptions.

Appendix A — sketch of the smoothing controller algorithm (pseudocode):
- Input: per-tenant envelope E_t (guaranteed_g, smoothing_pct, max_lease_dur), pool capacity C, current_allocations A_t
- Every control tick (10s):
  1) compute pool_free = C - sum(A_t.guaranteed) - reserved_headroom
  2) available_for_broker = max(0, pool_free - safety_margin)
  3) assign brokerable_leases up to available_for_broker honoring each E_t.max_share and preemption constraints
  4) monitor p95/p99 per-tenant; if any p99 > bound -> reduce smoothing_pct across tenants by delta and preempt oldest brokered leases

Appendix B — sample UI copy for console:
- "Turn on transient leasing to improve pool utilization and lower cost for non-critical workloads. Only enabled pools will participate. You can set the maximum percent of your reservation that may be leased out and the minimum buffer to preserve for critical traffic."

Next steps:
- Engineering: spike on lease ledger implementation and preemption latency budget (owner: Tomás).
- Product: customer interviews to validate pricing tolerance (owner: Aisha).
- Legal: draft contract addendum for opt-in behavior (owner: Nora).
